ai.mechanism: No mechanism can be established. The packet contains a single large USDC outflow (50,000,000.05 USDC, ~$50,000,000) removing 77.47% of the drained address's balance, with no call trace, no permission or role change, no failed-authorisation signal, no oracle or reentrancy evidence, and no protocol or instrument identified.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified. The holder of 0xa9d1e08c7793af67e9d92fe308d5697fb81d3e43 bears the balance reduction, but no protocol, depositor base or integrator is shown to be exposed.
ai.narrative: An address moved 50,000,000.05 USDC out in one transaction, taking 77.47% of what it held. That is the entire evidence. There is no protocol attached, no integrator exposure listed, and nothing in the packet showing the transfer was unauthorised: no hijacked admin role, no reinitialisation, no price distortion, no reentrant call. A round-figure fifty-million stablecoin transfer draining most of a balance is exactly what an exchange hot-wallet rebalance, treasury sweep or bridge settlement looks like. Absent authorisation evidence, treating this as an exploit would be a guess, so no loss path is supported.
